---
title: "Resources"
order: 116
---

This module introduces no new regulation, standard, or framework, and no new source was
fetched for it. Its entire job is crosswalking ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure
Library) vocabulary — the learner's own professional background, never itself cited to a
specific AXELOS/PeopleCert publication anywhere in this curriculum — onto two mechanics
`quality-system-essentials` already built and locked. The two links below are the direct
inputs this module maps against; read either one for the actual process mechanics and
citations, which this module deliberately doesn't redevelop.

- **[Change control for regulated
  systems](../../quality-system-essentials/change-control-for-regulated-systems/index.qmd)** —
  the five-stage process (change request, impact and risk assessment, approval, implementation,
  verification) this module's first crosswalk maps ITIL's change enablement practice onto,
  including the regulatory grounding (21 CFR 606.100(b)) and the AABB (Association for the
  Advancement of Blood & Biotherapies) Process Control QSE (Quality System Essential) behind it.
  Read it for the actual citation decoder, verbatim regulatory text, and the full stage-by-stage
  mechanics this lesson references by name but doesn't re-quote.

- **[CAPA: root cause to effectiveness
  check](../../quality-system-essentials/capa-root-cause-to-effectiveness/index.qmd)** — the
  four-stage CAPA (corrective and preventive action) structure (root cause analysis, corrective
  action, preventive action, effectiveness check) this module's second crosswalk maps ITIL's
  problem management practice onto, including the regulatory grounding (21 CFR 606.100(c) and
  606.171(f)) and the AABB Process Improvement QSE behind it. Read it for the actual root-cause
  technique (5 Whys), the four required pieces of a real effectiveness check, and the three
  possible closure outcomes (close, extend, reopen) this lesson references but doesn't
  redevelop.
